sections.text: As per RBI Master Direction on KYC 2024 Section 4.2, any customer with annual income exceeding ₹10,00,000 shall be categorized as 'Low Risk'. Such customers are eligible for expedited onboarding and simplified due diligence. Customers with income between ₹5,00,000 and ₹10,00,000 are 'Medium Risk'. All others are 'High Risk'.
regulatory_refs: RBI Master Direction on KYC 2024 Section 4.2

sections.text: Low Risk customers require KYC refresh every 5 years. Medium Risk every 3 years. High Risk every 1 year. As per RBI guidelines, any trigger event (large transaction, address change) mandates immediate re-KYC.
regulatory_refs: RBI Master Direction on KYC 2024 Section 4.5

sections.text: In compliance with RBI circular RBI/2023-24/85, all loan applications above ₹50,00,000 require enhanced due diligence including physical verification of residence and business premises. Applications above ₹1,00,00,000 additionally require a site visit report from an empanelled valuer.
Interest rates are determined based on customer risk score. Low Risk customers (as per KYC Policy Section 4.2) receive a 0.5% discount on the applicable card rate.

As mandated by RBI guidelines, all KYC records must be preserved for a minimum of 10 years from the date of account closure. Transaction records must be retained for 10 years. Loan documents for 12 years after repayment. CCTV footage for 90 days.
regulatory_refs: RBI Master Direction on KYC 2024 Section 5.0

sections.text: The system shall flag any transaction exceeding ₹10,00,000 in a newly opened account (less than 30 days old) for manual review. This threshold aligns with RBI circular RBI/2024-25/42 on mule account prevention.

Customers have the right to access their personal data within 30 days of request, as per RBI guidelines on digital lending and data protection. A nominal fee of ₹100 may be charged for physical copies.
